findings.detail: Rechecked original and current chapter: Portuguese/English speech and the tomato/potato pun retain the marked italic emphasis in Russian in their exact source positions.

source_anchor.quote: “Yeah, tomato, *potato*,” Max jokes, butchering the phrase ‘*tomato, tomato*’ (*to-may-to, to-mah-to*) on purpose.

translation_anchor.quote: «Ну да, помидор, *картошка*», — шутит Макс, нарочно коверкая выражение «*tomato, tomato*» (*то-мэй-тоу, то-ма-тоу*).

findings.detail: The prior awkward Russian calque describing tears escaping eyes was replaced with natural Russian while preserving that the yawning caused the tears.

source_anchor.quote: Few tears escape his eyes as he does so.

translation_anchor.quote: При этом у него на глазах выступает несколько слезинок.

findings.detail: Inline 'What?' speech is now enclosed in Russian quotation marks consistent with surrounding prose, rather than a misplaced em dash. Checked surrounding exchange and adjacent reported dialogue.

source_anchor.quote: “What?” he asks, not really expecting Max to repeat himself.

translation_anchor.quote: «Что?» — спрашивает он, особо не надеясь, что Макс повторит.
